newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA ROMP TO FIFTH CONSECUTIVE VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA ROMP TO FIFTH CONSECUTIVE VICTORY.

text.p: Australia, fired by an incisive new ball burst from Andrew Bichel and Jason Gillespie, completed their build up to the first test against South Africa with a fifth consecutive win on Tuesday.

The touring team cruised to a 79-run victory against a Transvaal Invitation XI at the Elkah Stadium, scoring 261 for seven in their 45 overs and dismissing the local side for 182 with three overs left.
The game was over as a contest by the 10th over of Transvaal's reply when wicketkeeper Nic Pothas was caught off Bichel without scoring, reducing his side to 29 for five.

Gillespie picked up two wickets but it was Bichel who did the real damage, removing test player Adam Bacher for three and highly rated youngsters Neil McKenzie (15) and Pothas to finish with three for 21.
There were only two stands of substance for the home side, firstly between Transvaal all-rounder Andrew Hall and Johannesburg schoolboy Solly Ndima.
They put on 53 for the sixth wicket, Ndima making 35 from 41 balls with six boundaries before having his middle stump removed by Greg Blewett.
Transvaal captain Clive Eksteen made 42 from 64 balls and added 54 for the ninth wicket with Wayne Kidwell, who finished 30 not out.
Earlier, Justin Langer (63) and Matthew Elliott (69) laid the foundation for Australia's challenging total by putting on 117 for the second wicket.
The tempo was lifted when Michael Bevan (49) and Matthew Hayden (47) smashed 98 for the fourth wicket in 11 overs.
The Invitation side gained a small measure of respite when Hall and Kidwell shared four wickets for four runs at the end of the innings.
Australia have now won all five games ahead of the first of three tests against South Africa, starting in Johannesburg on Friday.
